- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk aversion fading.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply “lag correction”: reduce forecast 2–5% in next 2–3 periods.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days moving toward historical mean), model often fails to catch it; dampen forecast slope by 10–20% in subsequent periods.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; apply “sentiment smoothing”: average sentiment over 3–5 days before adjusting forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast with sentiment trend only if sentiment persists for 3+ days.
